limitations: Native discovery adds only scratch preparation queries (inverseFront/inverseForces, previewFront/previewRear, reusable force-result object); extra preparation changes scratch cache stamps. One controller and one physical plant call occur per riding substep. The no-op control requires exact control outputs, plant inputs/outputs and all nonscratch physical state over both steps; it does not claim unchanged scratch stamps.
The native front interval uses the existing projected combined-slip 17 samples and its existing 97% margin; the held rear value is the original one-substep preview at early prior Fx.

Request interval includes yaw correction and differs from the conditional front-plus-held-rear force-to-acceleration interval. Neither is a solved steady two-axle equilibrium or an immediately delivered force guarantee.
Original trim anti-windup still compares admitted magnitude to the original recovery scalar; its literal law is retained, not redesigned for the signed interval.
Actual counterfactual commands pass the original inverse, trim, max bar, bar slew, pedal allocation and one finite-dt tyre/roll integration.
The second clone step repeats the saved input and contact values; it is a query-purity/control check, not a live suspension or AI continuation.
JSON fixture caveats remain limited to unused non-GP fields; recorded native commands/outputs and selected after-state values reproduce exactly.
